appliesTo.quote: Core IMPACTS Requirements (for incoming Summer 2024 students and any student updating their Catalog year to 2024-25):

olderCatalogs: Students on a 2023-2024 or older catalog year follow the old Core Areas A-F, published only in the archived catalogs (robots.txt disallows /archived-catalogs/, so not read here).

oneCourseOneArea.rule: One course may not satisfy two Core IMPACTS areas. It MAY also count for the ETHS attribute, the legislative requirements, and major requirements that list it.

quote.quote: Students may also take an additional course from this list to satisfy the Social Sciences area, but may not use one course to satisfy two Core IMPACTS areas.

noPassFail.quote: Courses taken to satisfy Core IMPACTS requirements, courses required for major, minor and certificate programs, courses that satisfy institutional requirements may not be taken as Pass/Fail.

thirtyHourRule.rule: After 30 earned hours, a student who has not finished Mathematics & Quantitative Skills or Communicating in Writing must take the next course toward it every term they enroll.

quotes.quote: students who have earned 30 hours but have not completed Mathematics & Quantitative Skills must enroll in the next course necessary to make progress toward completing this Area in every semester in which they take classes.

students who have earned 30 hours but have not completed Communicating in Writing must enroll in the next course necessary to make progress toward completing this Area in every semester in which they take classes.

Students are permitted to apply a maximum of 3 credit hours from one introductory (1002-, 2001-, or 2002-numbered) Modern Language course that carries the HUM attribute toward their Core IMPACTS area humanities requirement. Please note that: students may apply the maximum of 3 credit hours from one 1002-, 2001-, or 2002-numbered Modern Language course toward their Core IMPACTS Area humanities requirement only if that course carries the HUM attribute. students may not apply any credits from more than one 1002-, 2001-, or 2002-numbered Modern Language course toward their Core IMPACTS Area humanities requirement regardless of whether or not the course(s) carry the HUM attribute. students who apply the maximum of 3 credit hours from one introductory (1002-, 2001-, or 2002-numbered) Modern Language course carrying the HUM attribute toward their Core IMPACTS Area humanities requirement must satisfy the remaining 3 credit hours required to complete the Core IMPACTS area humanities requirement by applying credit hours from courses carrying the HUM attribute OTHER THAN introductory (1002-, 2001-, or 2002-numbered) Modern Language courses.

Transfer students are asked to please be aware that when they see courses on their GT record that are listed with an "X" in the number (JAPN 10X2, for example) it means that these are transfer courses and although they were not equated exactly with a GT course, they may have been accepted to meet a Core IMPACTS Area such as Arts, Humanities & Ethics and Social Sciences. howToUse: Illinois reads gen-ed membership from each course's genEd tags (RawIllinoisCourse.genEd -> CourseFacts.genEd and IllinoisCourse.tags, lib/planner/illinois-data.ts) and maps a requirement label to the tags it accepts with GENED_MAP / genEdForLabel. For Georgia Tech, set each course's genEd to tagsByCourse[code] ?? [] when building the course file, and use labelToTags as the Georgia Tech GENED_MAP (school-keyed, not merged into the Illinois map).

Georgia Tech degree pages print every core area as its own heading with real course rows (CS 1371; MATH 1552; HIST 2111 or ...; ENGL 1101 + 1102), so most of the core parses as ordinary required/choose blocks with no gen-ed handling at all.

Only three placeholder rows need tags: "Any HUM" (6) -> HUM, "Any SS" (9) -> SS, "Lab Science" (4 each, usually twice) -> Core IMPACTS: Lab Science. They are hours rows with no course, the shape illinois-data.ts reads as { kind: 'hours', hours, genEd: genEdForLabel(label) }.

MUST GATE: adaptIllinoisPrograms runs withCampusGenEd on every program, and a program without an Illinois campus table gets an appended "General Education Requirements (campus)" area holding Illinois categories and the Illinois third-semester language requirement. No Georgia Tech page has that table, so every Georgia Tech degree would get it. Skip withCampusGenEd (and genEdRulesFromText / GENED_CAMPUS_SIZE) when the school is gatech.

exclusiveGroup: all seven Core IMPACTS areas share ONE ledger at Georgia Tech (a course counts for one area only; see oneCourseOneArea). The Illinois rule (each category its own ledger, Cultural Studies exclusive) does not fit. ETHS and the legislative tags are separate ledgers that may reuse a core course.
Wellness is a 2-hour required area on every degree page ("Wellness Requirement": APPH 1040 or 1050 or 1060) and counts on top of the 120-hour minimum.

The legislative requirement has no hours. Check it as a rule over the plan (has the student a GT HIST 2111/2112, and a GT INTA 1200/POL 1101/PUBP 3000?) and otherwise tell the student about the non-credit exams; do not book hours for it.
